## Direction

Grounding assumption: this is a mobile settings screen for a meditation app's daily practice — session length, reminders, guidance voice, ambient sound, closing bell, account. The person opening it isn't shopping for a feature; they're adjusting something they already do every day. The screen should read like tuning an instrument you know, not configuring software.

## Design plan

**Color**
- Paper `#EDEAE2` — warm stone, not yellowed cream; the base surface
- Ink `#2A2823` — warm charcoal-black for all text
- Line `#D9D4C8` — hairline dividers, input borders
- Moss `#55705C` — the one accent; active toggles, selected values
- Brass `#A78859` — secondary, used only on sound/bell-related controls, never on toggles

**Type**
One family: a low-contrast old-style text serif with true italics and old-style tabular figures (numbers should feel handwritten, not tabular-grid). One scale, sentence case throughout, nothing set in caps:
- Display 28/34, medium — the summary line
- Section 16/22, medium — group names
- Body 17/26, regular — row labels and descriptions
- Caption 13/18, regular — helper text, timestamps

**Layout**
Single column, left-aligned, max width ~420px (mobile-first), line lengths under ~34 characters for the display line. No cards, no shadows, no rounded rectangles except the toggle switch itself. Hairline rules separate three groups that follow the actual shape of a sitting — before, during, after — rather than generic "General / Notifications / Account" buckets:

```
‹ Back

10 minutes, guided,
with an evening bell.

──────────────────────
Begin
  Remind me to practice    ●–○
    Every day at 7:30 am    Change

──────────────────────
Practice
  Session length            10 min   Change
  Voice guidance            ●–○
  Background sound          Rain     Change

──────────────────────
Close
  Closing bell              Temple bowl  Change
  End with a reflection     ●–○

──────────────────────
Account              Priya K.        ›
Subscription          Plus           ›
Data & privacy                       ›

Sign out
```

**Principles**
- The screen opens by stating your current practice as a sentence, not a title — "Settings" the word never needs to appear.
- Structure mirrors a sitting's arc (begin → practice → close), so grouping is load-bearing, not decorative.
- One accent color, spent on the things you actually change often (toggles); a second, quieter accent marks sound controls only.
- Account/subscription/sign-out are demoted to the bottom in caption weight — administrative, not the point of the screen.

## Self-review

My first instinct was cream background + serif display + terracotta accent — this is the generic "calm app" default and also collides with Claude's own accent, so I moved to a cooler stone/moss palette instead. I also nearly grouped settings as "General / Sound / Notifications," which is the templated IA for any settings screen regardless of subject; reorganizing around begin/practice/close is specific to what a meditation session actually is. I dropped an ALL-CAPS "SETTINGS" eyebrow and any middle-dot metadata strings — the summary sentence does that job in plain language instead.

## Screen copy

**Header:** `Back` · summary line, generated from current values: *"10 minutes, guided, with an evening bell."*

**Begin**
- Remind me to practice — toggle. When on: *"Every day at 7:30 am"* + `Change`. When off: *"Turn on to get a nudge each day."*
- Reminder time screen: title `Reminder time`, buttons `Save` / `Cancel`

**Practice**
- Session length — *"10 min"* + `Change`. Picker options: `5 min · 10 min · 15 min · 20 min · 30 min · Custom…`
- Voice guidance — toggle. Helper text: *"A quiet voice marks the start, midpoint, and end."*
- Background sound — *"Rain"* + `Change`. Options: `Silence · Rain · Ocean · Wind · Bowls`

**Close**
- Closing bell — *"Temple bowl"* + `Change`. Options: `Temple bowl · Chime · Gong · Silence`
- End with a reflection — toggle. Helper text: *"A short prompt to note how the sitting felt."*

**Account** (caption weight, quiet)
- `Account` — Priya K. ›
- `Subscription` — Plus ›
- `Data & privacy` ›
- `Sign out`

**Error and empty states**
- Notifications blocked: *"Notifications are off for this app. Turn them on in your phone's settings to get reminders."*
- Voice pack fails to load: *"Couldn't load the guide voice. Check your connection and try again."* Button: `Try again`
- No sounds downloaded (offline): *"No sounds downloaded yet. Connect to add rain, ocean, and bowls."*

## Motion

One moment only: tapping `Change` on the closing bell plays a soft concentric ripple around the row, timed to the actual bell sample, like a bowl being struck. Everywhere else is static. Under reduced motion, the ripple is replaced with a single fade instead of a scale/expand.

# Rockies SAR — Design Direction

**Subject & audience:** A volunteer search-and-rescue team wants people to understand what joining actually involves — fitness and availability requirements, training and certification, the on-call commitment — and to know the concrete steps to apply. The audience is self-selecting: hikers, climbers, skiers, EMTs, ham radio operators, dog handlers who are already outdoors-capable and want the real terms, not a recruitment pitch. The job of the page is to be honest and procedural, like a briefing, not aspirational.

## Color

| Name | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Quad Paper | `#EAEBE2` | background — the grey-green tone of old USGS topo map paper |
| Timberline | `#1E3329` | headlines, borders, primary text |
| Granite | `#55564F` | body text |
| Contour Tan | `#A99772` | contour-line rules, dividers, subtle fills |
| Rescue Orange | `#E2531B` | one accent — CTA and mission-alert elements only |

Orange is the color of SAR gear itself (blaze vests, avalanche probes, rescue packs), so it's earned, not decorative — and it's used in exactly two places so it keeps its urgency.

## Type

One family: **Overpass** — a grotesk derived from US highway/trail signage, so it already carries the right vernacular. Black/Bold for headlines, Regular for body, set left-aligned with a line length under 70 characters.

For actual data — timestamps, GPS coordinates, elevation figures, response-time stats — use a monospace (**IBM Plex Mono**), but only where real numbers appear. No decorative eyebrow labels in monospace.

## Layout

Left-aligned throughout — this reads as a field manual or checklist, which matches how SAR teams actually operate: protocol, not mood. Thin tan contour-line rules stand in for section dividers, echoing the terrain rather than decorating the page.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [faint topo contour lines, full width]   │
│                                           │
│ 2:47 AM.                                 │
│ Someone is missing on Bear Creek Trail.  │
│ Fourteen volunteers are already moving.  │
│                                           │
│ We're an all-volunteer SAR team serving  │
│ the [range name]. Here's what it takes   │
│ to join us.          [See how to join →] │
├─── contour rule ──────────────────────────┤
│ WHAT WE DO                               │
│ wilderness search · technical rope       │
│ rescue · avalanche · swiftwater · K9     │
├─── contour rule ──────────────────────────┤
│ WHAT IT TAKES                            │
│ fitness standard, availability, annual   │
│ training hours, on-call commitment       │
├─── contour rule ──────────────────────────┤
│ HOW TO JOIN                              │
│ 1  Attend an info session                │
│ 2  Ride along on a training exercise     │
│ 3  Apply                                 │
│ 4  Complete certifications (WFR, radio)  │
│ 5  Field evaluation                      │
│ 6  Join the callout roster               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Numbers only appear in "How to Join" because that's a genuine sequence — nowhere else on the page gets numbered markers.

## Principles

- The page reads like a field log, not a brochure — real timestamps and terrain vocabulary, no adventure-marketing gloss.
- Orange means "this matters now," reserved strictly for the alert line and the apply CTA.
- Contour lines are structural (dividers, hero texture), not decorative — they're literally the terrain these volunteers work in.
- Copy is plain and specific: buttons say what happens ("See how to join," "Apply now"), not "Learn More →."

**What I steered away from:** the default instinct here is a cream background with a warm serif and a terracotta accent, or a big glossy mountain photo behind a "Join Our Team" banner. Both are template moves that could sit on any outdoor-brand site. Grounding the palette in topo-map paper and reserving orange for actual SAR gear color, and opening on a callout log instead of a hero photo, ties every choice back to how this specific team actually works.

# Design direction: Rockies volunteer SAR recruitment site

## Grounding

Subject: a volunteer search-and-rescue team operating in the Colorado/Rockies backcountry. Audience: capable outdoorspeople — hikers, climbers, skiers, EMTs, ham radio operators — deciding whether to commit real hours to something with real stakes. The page's job isn't to "sell" SAR, it's to answer, credibly and quickly: what does this team do, am I the kind of person they need, and what's the actual path to becoming a member. Trust and competence matter more than polish here — this reads closer to a field manual or a fire department's site than a startup landing page.

## Plan

**Color**
- `#1C2A24` — spruce-shadow, near-black green-charcoal (night approach, deep timber). Base dark.
- `#EDE7D8` — topo-paper buff. Not cream-for-cream's-sake — it's the actual color of a folded USGS quad.
- `#5B4A34` — contour-line brown, used for hairline map contours and rules.
- `#B8460E` — blaze/safety-orange, the real color of SAR gear (packs, flagging tape, avalanche shovels). Justified by the subject, not decoration — and deliberately not the warm-clay `#D97757` terracotta.
- `#3A5A6B` — alpine-lake blue-grey, secondary accent for water/weather info.
- `#F4F1E8` — near-white for body text on dark.

Two-value system: most pages sit on the topo-paper buff with charcoal ink; the hero and one "active callout" section invert to spruce-shadow with buff/orange, like night operations versus daylight fieldwork.

**Type**
- Headlines: **Zilla Slab** (bold/black weights) — a slab serif with the blunt, chiseled feel of routed trail signage and wood waymarkers. Used big, tight tracking, never italicized for emphasis.
- Body/UI/labels: **IBM Plex Sans Condensed** — built for dense technical readouts, reads like text on a GPS unit or a radio log. Handles small data (coordinates, elevations, dates) without feeling like a generic UI font.
- No monospace, no all-caps labels, no tracked-out eyebrows. Numbers (elevation, coordinates, dates) get their own small treatment in Plex Condensed tabular figures instead.

**Layout**
- Single-column, left-aligned, max ~640px measure for body copy — a field-manual page, not a marketing spread.
- The hero is a full-bleed line-art topographic map of the team's actual operating range (a real, specific Rockies subrange — pick one, e.g., the Sawatch or the Front Range) with a thin plotted line showing a rescue route. Headline sits directly on the map, not in a card.

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ░░░ contour lines, faint, full-bleed ░░░  │
│                                             │
│   You already know these mountains.        │
│   We need people who do.                   │
│                                             │
│   [Base camp: Buena Vista, CO — 8,000 ft]  │
│                                             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- Below the fold: a short "what we do" paragraph, then the join process rendered as a waypoint trail — this is a genuine sequence (info session → field training → probation → certified member), so waypoint markers along a drawn trail line are earned, not decorative.
```
●───────●───────●───────●
Info    Field   6-mo    Certified
session training probation member
```
- A "recent callout" log entry (real-feeling, e.g., date / location / outcome) instead of a stats-bar hero — this is the single most characteristic artifact of the org and doubles as proof of activity.
- Requirements and gear expectations presented as a plain list, not icon cards — this content is a checklist, not a feature grid.
- Footer holds the base coordinates, radio callsign, and a direct contact — quiet, functional, no social icons row.

**Principles**
- Every visual device (contours, waypoints, coordinates) is something SAR teams actually use — nothing decorative gets added on top.
- One bold color, blaze-orange, used sparingly for the one or two things that matter most (the primary CTA, the trail line).
- Copy speaks the way a team briefing does: direct, specific, no recruitment-brochure language.

## Review against the brief

Checking against the generic default I'd otherwise produce: a warm cream page, big serif headline, terracotta CTA button, numbered "01/02/03" feature cards, all-caps "OUR MISSION" eyebrow, rounded SaaS cards with soft shadows for "why join us."

Revisions made to avoid that:
- Swapped the cream+terracotta pairing for topo-paper buff + blaze-orange — visually similar in temperature but sourced from the subject (actual SAR equipment color) rather than the generic AI palette, and shifted a couple of notches away from the flagged hex.
- Replaced the default "big stat + small label" hero with a topo map plus a real callout log entry — more specific to this org and harder to template.
- Kept numbering *only* for the join pipeline, because it's a genuine sequence; dropped the instinct to number the "why join us" reasons, which aren't sequential — those are set as a plain list instead.
- Removed all-caps labels and eyebrows throughout; section headers are sentence case and named for what they contain ("How you join," "What we ask of you"), not templated section chrome.

## Copy direction (examples)

- Hero: "You already know these mountains. We need people who do." (not "Join Our Team — Save Lives")
- CTA: "Come to an info session" (states exactly what happens — not "Get Started" or "Learn More →")
- Requirements intro: "This isn't a weekend commitment. Here's what it actually takes." — direct, no apology, no sales tone.
- Empty/edge state (e.g., no upcoming sessions listed): "No sessions scheduled right now. Email us and we'll let you know when the next one's set." — practical next step, not a vague "check back soon."

This gives you a site that looks like it belongs to people who actually go out at 2 a.m. in the snow, not a generic nonprofit template.

# Settings — Design Direction

## Grounding

A meditation app's settings screen isn't a sales surface — it's the room the user tidies before or after sitting. The recognizable objects of the practice aren't lotus flowers or gradients; they're the tools that measure and mark a session: a mala's beads for counting, a bell for opening and closing, an incense stick burning down to mark time. I'm using the **mala and the bell** as the structural language of the page, since settings genuinely are: a set of discrete, countable groups (beads) that you move through in order to configure how your sessions sound and run (the bell tuning them).

## Plan

**Color**
- `#25252A` — warm charcoal-plum, base background (a dim room at dusk, not flat black)
- `#EDEAE2` — unbleached paper, primary text
- `#8B8A8F` — warm grey, secondary text / descriptions
- `#3A393E` — raised surface for inputs, barely lifted off the base
- `#B9663A` — ember (a lit incense tip, more brick than orange), used only for the active/on state and one focal accent
- `#5C6B5C` — quiet moss, used only for success/confirmation states (saved, exported)

**Type**

# A field-briefing site, not a nonprofit template

Search-and-rescue in the Rockies runs on topo maps, radio callouts, and hard specifics about terrain and gear — the site should read like a briefing document, not a donation-drive landing page. Here's the direction.

## Color
- `#2B3A3A` — slate-spruce (near-black base, has a green cast instead of true black)
- `#EDEAE0` — weathered paper (background, like a topo map printed on field stock)
- `#5C7A6A` — forest contour (secondary text, section fills)
- `#3D5A73` — alpine dusk (links, structural lines)
- `#D64B0F` — rescue orange (single accent — this is literally the color of SAR packs, tape flags, and helicopter gear, not a decorative pick)
- `#8A8172` — trail dust (muted labels, captions)

## Type
- **Display: a condensed, slightly rough-edged grotesque** (direction: something like Founders Grotesk Condensed or National 2 Condensed) — set tight and heavy, like stenciled lettering on a rescue cache box. Used at large size for section openers only.
- **Body/UI: a plain, utilitarian grotesque** (direction: Suisse Int'l or Inter) at a slightly wider tracking than default — legible at a glance, the way trailhead signage is designed to be read fast in bad light.
- One family pairing, no serif. Line length capped around 62–68 characters; body text left-aligned throughout, never centered — briefings and incident reports don't center text, and neither should this.

## Layout
Content is a single scrolling page, structured like a field manual rather than a marketing funnel: dense, functional, generous top/bottom margins between sections but narrow side margins, so it feels like a printed sheet, not a floating card stack.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [topo contour line art, hand-drawn  │
│   route tracing across the page]     │
│                                       │
│  Last winter we ran 41 callouts.     │  <- hero: a real
│  Most started with one radio call.   │     operational fact,
│                                       │     not a slogan
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  What the team does        (2 col,   │
│  Who we're looking for      left-    │
│                              aligned) │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  01  Fitness & interview             │  <- numbered: this
│  02  Orientation weekend             │     genuinely is a
│  03  Field training (14 weeks)       │     sequence
│  04  Certification & first rotation  │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Apply to join   [single orange CTA] │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  If someone is missing right now,    │
│  call dispatch: [phone] — footer     │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The hero is a thin, hand-traced topo contour line that animates once on load — as if a route is being plotted across the mountain — then settles. That's the one deliberate motion moment; nothing else on the page animates on scroll.

## Principles
1. **Specificity over sell.** Real numbers (callouts last year, weeks of training, elevation gain on the fitness test) instead of mission-statement language.
2. **Orange means one thing.** It's reserved entirely for the "Apply" action, echoing actual SAR high-vis gear — never used as decoration elsewhere on the page.
3. **Numbers only where there's a real sequence.** The training pipeline is genuinely ordered, so it's the one place numbered steps belong.
4. **Left-aligned, field-manual rhythm.** No centered hero text, no rounded cards, no drop shadows — flat, ruled sections like pages in a logbook.
5. **The failure/empty states speak plainly.** An unfilled application field says what's missing and why it matters ("We need an emergency contact — this is who we call if you're hurt on a callout"), not generic validation text.

This avoids the two defaults this brief could easily fall into: a warm-cream/serif nonprofit look, or a rounded SaaS-card volunteer-signup template. Both would flatten what's actually distinctive here — that this is technical, terrain-based, safety-critical work, and the site should feel like it was built by people who've actually stood at a trailhead in the dark with a radio.

# Search & Rescue Recruitment Site — Design Direction

## The subject, pinned down
A volunteer mountain SAR team in the Rockies, speaking to people who are already comfortable outdoors — hikers, climbers, ex-military, medics — and need to know exactly what joining costs them in time and training, and what it gives back. The job of the page is orientation, literally: tell someone where they stand and what the route to becoming a team member looks like.

## Design plan

**Color**
- `Granite #2E3235` — near-black, but read as wet rock at dusk, not a stock "off-black." Primary text and dark UI surfaces.
- `Snowline #F3F4F1` — cool, slightly grey white (paper/snow), not the warm cream default. Base background.
- `Glacier #7C97A3` — muted blue-grey, distant peaks. Secondary text, hairlines, inactive states.
- `Rescue Orange #E4572E` — the actual color of SAR gear (packs, vests, tape). One functional accent only: CTAs, the "you are here" marker, active states.
- `Lichen #6B7A5E` — muted alpine green. Used sparingly for confirmation/success moments (e.g. "Application received").

**Type**
- Headlines: a sturdy, low-contrast slab serif (Zilla Slab or similar) — the same family of letterform used on USGS topo map labels and trailhead signage. Gives the page a mapped, engraved feel instead of an editorial one.
- Body/UI: Public Sans — the humanist grotesque built for U.S. government services. It reads as functional and trustworthy, which fits an emergency-service register better than a startup sans.
- Data only (coordinates, elevation, radio channel): a monospace, used exclusively where real data appears — never as decorative labeling.

**Layout**
- Left-aligned throughout, line lengths under 75 characters. No centered hero.
- Hero: a topographic contour map of real Rockies terrain, hairline-drawn, with a single "YOU ARE HERE" pin — the actual convention on trailhead maps — placed at the reader's position, with the headline set beside it, not over it.
- Section dividers are contour-interval rules: thin lines between minor content blocks, a heavier rule every fifth section, exactly like index contours on a topo map — so the weight of a divider tells you how big a break it is.
- The "how to join" section is a sequence, so it gets a linear device — but it's an ascending trail elevation profile, not numbered circles. Each stage of joining sits at a marker along the climbing line, tying "steps to join" to "steps up the mountain."

```
[contour hero, pin + headline]
------------------------------- (light rule)
What volunteers actually do
------------------------------- (light rule)
What it takes (fitness / gear / time)
=============================== (heavy rule)
The route to the team  (elevation-profile steps)
------------------------------- (light rule)
Questions people ask
------------------------------- (light rule)
Apply
```

**Principles**
- Every structural device (contours, elevation profile, the pin) is a real SAR/map tool repurposed for navigation, not decoration borrowed from elsewhere.
- One animated moment only: the hero contour lines trace in like a plotted route, ending with the pin dropping into place. Nothing else moves on load; button presses just deepen in color, like ink soaking into paper.
- Copy stays plain and specific — real elevations, real training names, real time commitments — never marketing language.

## Checked against the generic defaults
- Not cream + serif + terracotta: base is cool grey-white, accent is safety-orange tied to actual gear, not a warm clay borrowed from elsewhere.
- Not near-black + acid accent: background is light; the dark tone is a text color grounded in "wet granite," not a moody dark-mode shell.
- Not broadsheet hairlines: the rules vary in weight on purpose (contour intervals), so they carry information rather than imitate a newspaper.
- Not uniform rounded cards: there are no cards here — content sits in map-like bands separated by contour rules.
- No ALL-CAPS eyebrows, no dot-joined meta strings, no "→" on links, no accent-one-word headlines. CTA reads "Start your application," and the confirmation after submitting says "Application received," not "Submitted."

## What the page says, section by section
- **Hero:** "You are here." beside the pin, then a one-line headline naming the actual range covered — e.g. "Front Range Search & Rescue trains volunteers to find people before the weather does." No stat block, no supporting stat row.
- **What volunteers do:** short, concrete paragraph — night searches, exposure, technical rope evacuation, the radio call that ends a mission — not a mission-statement paragraph.
- **What it takes:** a plain two-column list — fitness and availability expected of you, versus gear and training the team provides — so applicants can self-select honestly before applying.
- **The route to the team:** Apply → Orientation hike → Technical training (navigation, wilderness first aid, rope systems) → Field evaluation → Active roster, each sitting at a point along the rising trail line, with the elevation gain and rough time commitment (weeks/months) labeled at each marker.
- **Questions people ask:** conversational Q&A — real questions like "Do I need to already know how to climb?" answered directly, no corporate FAQ tone.
- **Apply:** a short form, one CTA — "Start your application" — and nothing else competing for attention on the page's only orange button outside the hero pin.

- Body copy: **Source Serif 4** (Regular/Medium) — a plain, legible book serif, guidebook rather than editorial-magazine in feel
Two families, clearly distinct roles: condensed grotesk for structure, serif for reading. Body measure kept under 70 characters; serif body gets slightly more line-height than the condensed labels.

**Layout**
The page is built as an actual route: a continuous elevation-profile line runs down the page as a spine, and each content section is a waypoint on it — elevation rising as commitment deepens, ending at the summit ("Active Member"). This isn't decorative; the training pipeline really is a fixed sequence, so numbering/waypoints are earned here, not defaulted to.

```

11,800 |                                    ● SUMMIT — Active member,
       |                              ___/‾‾   on the callout roster
10,600 |                        ●____/       Certification & first callouts
```

1. The elevation profile is real information architecture (progress = altitude), not texture.
2. Orange appears only where it means something functional: the button, the current-position marker — never as brand decoration.

## The page

**Hero.** Snowfield background, left-aligned. Headline in Barlow Condensed states what the team actually does, plainly — no single accented word:
> We look for people in the dark, above treeline, in weather nobody else is out in.

Subhead in Source Serif: one sentence naming the team's home range and its relationship to the county sheriff's office (SAR teams operate under a sheriff's authority in Colorado — worth stating for credibility). Directly beneath, the elevation-profile graphic begins and doubles as the page's navigation — each waypoint is a jump link. A plain sentence sits near it instead of a stat card: "Next orientation meeting: first Tuesday of the month, Nederland fire hall, 7pm." — real and specific beats a big impressive number.

**Trailhead — What we do.** Plain paragraphs on wilderness search, technical rope rescue, avalanche response, mutual aid callouts. No icon grid, no cards.

**9,400 ft — Training academy.** A genuine syllabus, numbered because it's a real 14-week sequence: wilderness first aid, navigation and radio procedure, rope systems, avalanche awareness, litter evacuation.

**10,600 ft — Certification & first callouts.** Probationary period, paired with a mentor, first supervised missions.

**Summit — Active member.** The single Blaze-orange button: "Start your application." No arrow glyph appended, no ALL-CAPS label above it.

**Footer** sits on a Timberline `#33463A` band with Ridge White text: non-emergency contact, meeting location, and — because it's a genuine safety necessity for this subject — a plain line: "If someone is missing right now, call 911."

No hover flourishes on cards, no staggered section entrances. Reduced-motion users get the finished line with the dot jumping to position, no animated draw.

## Design plan

**Color**
- `#EDEAE3` — Stone (page background, warm grey-stone paper, not cream)

```
|  ───────────────────────────────────────
|  Guide voice                       Mara
|  ───────────────────────────────────────
|  Breath pacing                     Slow

| Sound
```

## Proposal

This is a settings screen for a meditation app — the "Mara" system I'll call it here for authorship purposes only. Audience: people who already practice, opening this screen mid-routine (often at night or pre-dawn) to adjust one specific thing, not browse. Its job: let them find and change a setting in one glance, without the screen itself producing the low-grade anxiety that dense settings UIs usually do. I'll ground the design in the physical objects of a meditation practice — mala beads, struck bells, paper lanterns — rather than in generic "wellness app" signifiers.

## Design plan

**Color**
- `#1C2230` — Ink: screen background, deep slate-navy rather than true black
- `#E8E1D3` — Parchment: the single raised surface holding all settings rows
- `#5C6E5A` — Moss: active/on states, confirmations
- `#C9A227` — Brass: the one accent, used only for the struck-bell ripple micro-interaction
- `#8B8375` — Stone: secondary text, dividers
- `#3A2E22` — Ink-brown: primary text on parchment

**Type**
- Piazzolla (serif) — screen title and the five section names only. Warm, slightly inky oldstyle serif, set at a size and weight that reads as furniture, not marketing.
- Public Sans (sans) — every row label, value, and button. Neutral and legible at small sizes, doesn't compete with the serif.
No eyebrows, no all-caps, no letter-spacing tricks on either face.

**Layout**
One continuous parchment panel on the ink background, left-aligned throughout (this is a scan-and-tap utility screen — centering or justifying it would fight its function). Rows are grouped by hairline rules only where a hairline groups *related* settings; groups are separated by whitespace, not boxes or shadows.

```
 Settings

 Practice
 ─────────────────────────
 Session length          20 min
 Guide voice              Mara
 Background sound         Rain
 Closing bell               ◐  ← mala-bead toggle

 Reminders
 ─────────────────────────
 Daily reminder    7:00 AM  ●
 Reminder days        Every day
 Quiet hours                 ◐

 Sound & feel
 ─────────────────────────
 Bell tone       Tibetan bowl
 Volume          ▬▬▬▬▬▬▭▭
 Haptic touch                ●

 Account
 ─────────────────────────
 Name                    Alex
 Subscription   renews Dec 4
 Download my data
 Sign out

 About
 ─────────────────────────
 Send feedback
 Privacy policy
 Version                 4.2.1
```

**Principles**
1. Toggles are a small bead sliding along a shallow groove, not a pill switch — a direct, literal reference to mala beads used for counting breath or mantra, the one motif that couldn't belong to any other app.
2. The single moment of motion: tapping a toggle sends one soft brass ripple outward from the bead, like a struck bowl, then it settles. Nothing else on the screen animates.
3. No numbered steps anywhere — these are independent settings, not a sequence, so no `01 / 02 / 03` markers.
4. Rows state their current value plainly (`20 min`, `Rain`, `Tibetan bowl`) so the screen doubles as a summary of the person's practice, not just a menu.

## Review against the brief

My first instinct was cream background + serif display + warm clay accent, which is the default I'd produce for almost any calm/wellness brief — so I dropped the clay accent entirely (`#C9A227` brass replaces it, and it's rationed to one interaction rather than spread across buttons and links) and moved the background off pure cream into ink-navy so the parchment panel reads as an object sitting on a surface, not the whole screen. I also nearly reached for numbered steps to group the five sections and for ALL-CAPS section eyebrows — cut both, since nothing here is sequential and the serif section names already carry enough weight on their own.

## Labels and button text

**Practice**
- Session length — *20 min*
- Guide voice — *Mara*
- Background sound — *Rain*
- Closing bell (toggle) — helper text on tap: "Rings softly in the last 10 seconds of your session."

**Reminders**
- Daily reminder (toggle + time) — *7:00 AM*
- Reminder days — *Every day*
- Quiet hours (toggle) — helper text: "Reminders stay off while you sleep."

**Sound & feel**
- Bell tone — *Tibetan bowl*
- Volume
- Haptic touch (toggle) — helper text: "A gentle pulse when a session ends."

**Account**
- Name
- Subscription — *renews December 4*
- Download my data (button) — opens a plain confirmation: "We'll prepare your data and notify you when it's ready. This can take up to 24 hours."
- Sign out (button)

**About**
- Send feedback (button)
- Privacy policy (link)
- Version — *4.2.1*

**Confirmation dialogs**
- Sign out dialog: "Sign out of Mara?" → buttons **Sign out** / **Cancel**
- Delete account dialog: "This deletes your practice history and can't be undone." → buttons **Delete account** / **Keep account**

Every button names the exact action it performs, and the word on the button reappears in whatever confirms it happened ("Sign out" → you're signed out, not "You have been logged out successfully").

# Settings screen — meditation app

**Proposal:** The audience is people already mid-practice with the app — they're opening settings between sits, often at night or right before/after meditating, and the job is to let them adjust things quickly without the screen fighting the calm they came in with. I'm grounding this in the feel of adjusting a well-made instrument you trust — a singing bowl's fittings, a timer's dial — rather than a typical app settings page.

## Design plan

**Color**
- `#211F1D` — warm graphite base (brown undertone, not tinted black)
- `#2B2825` — raised surface / row hover
- `#EDE8DE` — bone, primary text
- `#8C8579` — ash, secondary text and dividers
- `#B8935A` — aged brass, the single accent (active toggles, focus ring)

**Type**
- *Piazzolla* (serif) — section headers and row labels. Low-contrast, warm, unhurried strokes.
- *Karla* (grotesque sans) — values, descriptions, buttons. Rounded terminals keep it from feeling clinical next to the serif.

**Layout**
One continuous vertical list, not cards — each setting is a row: label left, control right, like reading dials across a panel.

```
Settings

Practice
────────────────────────────
Session length          20 min
Bell sound              Temple
Interval bells              ●

Reminders
────────────────────────────
Daily reminder          7:00 am
Gentle nudge                 ○

Sound & haptics
────────────────────────────
Background sound          Rain
Haptic pulse                 ●

Account
────────────────────────────
Sign out
Delete practice data
```
Left-aligned throughout; the divider is a hairline in ash, not brass — brass appears only where something is on. Section headers sit in sentence case, modest size, no tracking.

**Principles**
- One accent, spent only on "on" states and focus — everything else stays quiet.
- No cards, no shadows, no rounded chips: a row is a row, closed by a rule.
- Section headers are sentence case, not tracked-out caps.
- No numbering — nothing here is a sequence.

## Review against brief

Checked this against what a generic settings screen would produce: cream background + terracotta toggle, or dark mode with a single neon accent, sectioned into rounded cards with soft shadows, ALL CAPS section eyebrows. I avoided all four by using a warm (not cool-tinted) dark base with a brass accent instead of terracotta or neon, rows instead of cards, and sentence-case headers instead of tracked caps. **Section: Practice**
- Session length — 20 min
- Bell sound — Temple
- Interval bells (toggle)

**Section: Reminders**
- Daily reminder — 7:00 am
- Gentle nudge (toggle) — helper text: *A second, quieter reminder if you miss the first.*

**Section: Sound & haptics**
- Background sound — Rain
- Haptic pulse (toggle)

**Section: Account**
- Sign out
- Delete practice data

**Confirmation dialog (Delete practice data):**
- Body: "This removes your session history and streak. It can't be undone."
- Buttons: Cancel / Delete data

**Sign out confirmation:**
- Body: "You'll need to sign back in to keep your streak synced."
- Buttons: Cancel / Sign out

All buttons and toggles keep the same wording wherever they appear next — "Sign out" stays "Sign out," never "Log out" elsewhere; "Delete practice data" never shortens to "Delete" on a later screen.

## Concept

A settings screen for a meditation app is usually just an inventory of toggles — the generic default is a rounded-card list with icons and grey shadows, which reads like every other app's account page regardless of what it's for. The alternative here comes from the subject itself: a meditation session has a shape — you prepare, you sit, you close — so the settings mirror that arc instead of an arbitrary alphabetical or "account vs. app" grouping.

## Design plan

**Color**
- `#E7E4DB` — unbleached linen (base background, cooler and greyer than a cream/terracotta palette)
- `#2C2F2A` — soft ink (primary text, not pure black)
- `#6B7A5E` — moss (active states, toggles-on, selected values)
- `#8A7355` — worn bronze (the closing-bell accent — used once, on the "When you rise" section only)
- `#B7B2A3` — stone (dividers, secondary text, inactive toggle track)

**Type**
One family, two weights, no second typeface: **Source Serif 4** at a light-to-regular weight throughout. Serif everywhere avoids the "serif headline / sans body" template, and a serif's slower rhythm suits an app about slowing down. Section headers sit at the same size as row labels, just set in italic — no tracked-out caps, no eyebrow labels. Numerals (session length, times) get a slightly larger, tabular-figure treatment so they read as the one thing worth a glance.

**Layout**

## Grounding

The screen: settings for a meditation app, for someone already in the habit — adjusting session length, reminders, and sound rather than being sold the product. The job of this screen is to feel like tuning an instrument, not filling out a form.

## Design plan

**Color** — Avoiding the two default meditation-app palettes (cream + terracotta, or near-black + one bright accent), I grounded this in unglazed ceramic and cushion fabric instead:
- `#E7E2D8` — Ash Paper (background, warmer and greyer than the standard AI cream)
- `#2B2A26` — Soft Ink (text; warm charcoal, not a tinted near-black)
- `#9C7A3F` — Temple Brass (single accent — active states, the one toggle-on color)
- `#5B6650` — Moss (secondary, used only for the "on" fill behind brass, cushion-fabric tone)
- `#C9C2B2` — Ash Rule (hairline dividers)

**Type** — Two families, clearly distinct in register: **Newsreader** (a quiet literary serif, light weight, used only for the page title "Settings" and nothing else) paired with **Public Sans** for every label, value, and button — a humanist grotesque with enough warmth not to feel like dashboard chrome. No monospace anywhere; values like times and durations sit in the same sans as everything else.

**Layout** — A ledger, not a card list: a narrow left column carries the section name once, set beside its rows rather than stacked above them as an eyebrow. No rounded corners, no shadows, no icon chips.

```
  Settings

  Practice        Session length         20 minutes
                   Guide voice             Warm
                   Background sound        Rain
                   Bell at close           ● on
  ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Reminders        Daily reminder          ● on
                   Time                    7:00 AM
  ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Sound & touch    Bells during sitting    ○ off
                   Gentle vibration        ● on
  ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Account          Name        Asha Rao
                   Email       asha@mail.com
  ───────────────────────────────────────────────
                   Sign out
                   Delete account
```

Left-aligned throughout, generous vertical rhythm between rows (room to breathe), rule weight stays constant — no false hierarchy games.

**Principles** — One accent, one motion moment: when "Bell at close" is switched on, a single thin ring expands once from the toggle and fades, echoing a struck bowl — not a hover effect repeated on every row, just this one setting because it's the one that's literally about a sound. Everything else responds instantly with no animation at all.

The label-column ledger replaces the generic stacked-card-with-eyebrow pattern I'd default to, and the brass/moss pairing replaces the terracotta-on-cream combination that's become a tell for this exact kind of app. Kept sentence case and cut any "→" or middle-dot chrome since none of it does real work here.
